compiler-config.summary: Know what tsc checks, what it emits and what it never does at runtime. Then know the handful of options that change type safety, module output and build behaviour, including the defaults that changed in TypeScript 6.0.
points: Types are erased: tsc adds no runtime checks, emits even on errors unless `noEmitOnError` is set, and never polyfills APIs.

`strict` (on by default since TypeScript 6.0) bundles strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, strictFunctionTypes, strictBindCallApply, strictPropertyInitialization, noImplicitThis, useUnknownInCatchVariables and alwaysStrict. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` are separate opt-ins.
`target` controls emitted syntax; `lib` controls which API types exist. Raising `lib` without a polyfill only hides runtime crashes.
Under `module: "nodenext"`, relative imports need the runtime extension (`./b.js`). `paths` never rewrites emitted imports.
`isolatedModules`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` and `erasableSyntaxOnly` make tsc report code that single-file transpilers or Node's type stripping would get wrong.
Project references need `composite` and `tsc -b`. Plain `tsc -p` checks against whatever `.d.ts` files a referenced project last emitted.
TypeScript 6.0 defaults `types` to `[]`, enables `noUncheckedSideEffectImports`, ties `rootDir` to the tsconfig folder, and deprecates baseUrl, node10 resolution, ES5 targets and outFile.
traps: `exclude` does not keep a file out of the program if another file imports it.
`skipLibCheck` also skips your own hand-written `.d.ts` files.
Deleting `dist/` but keeping a `.tsbuildinfo` stored elsewhere makes the next incremental build emit nothing.
